title.rendered: Cushing man jailed on second domestic violence charge in Payne County

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

   STILLWATER — A Cushing man has been jailed on $20,000 bond pending a Sept. 16 preliminary hearing on a felony charge of abusing his girlfriend two months after he was placed on probation for abusing her in Payne County, court records show.    If convicted of domestic assault and battery as a subsequent offense, Kelly Michael Smith, 30, could be given up to a 10-year prison term and a $5,000 fine.    A neighbor had reported at about 2:08 am on July 11, 2025, a woman, who appeared to be “beat up and injured,” came to her house and asked for help, an affidavit alleged.    The woman “told officers that her live-in boyfriend, Kelly Smith, had assaulted her, and he would not stop,” Cushing Police Officer Carson Watts alleged in an affidavit. She had “a bruised and swollen face, left eye beginning to blacken and a large mark on her forehead with distinct lines,” the affidavit said.    “She told me that he had kicked her in her face while wearing boots,” the officer alleged in his affidavit.    Police were unable to find Smith at the residence where Officer Watts was bitten on the leg by a dog believed to be protecting her puppies, the affidavit said.    When the woman was asked if Smith might have left the house in their car, “she told me that the car was broken down in Tulsa. While searching the house, I did notice different items to be broken and thrown around the house, a broken mirror on the floor in the hallway and blood on the floor and bedspread.    “I told her that I would be taking pictures of the interior of the house, and she told me that she did not want me taking pictures of the house or her and did not want to talk about the incident any further. She was then taken to the hospital,” the officer alleged in his affidavit.    At the Cushing hospital, “With my body camera activated, I spoke with her again about what had happened. She showed me the boot prints on her forehead, left eye that was blackening and swollen, bite marks on her left forearm and right bicep area, as well as her scratched up knee.    “She told me that Kelly believed she was lying to him and hiding pictures from him. She said Kelly demanded to search her phone and laptop, which started the assault. She told me the assault had been ongoing for about four hours before she left the house…She said she had several opportunities to leave but kept hoping that Kelly would stop assaulting her,” the officer alleged in his affidavit.    “I then asked her if Kelly had choked or strangled her, and she told me that she no longer wanted to talk to me about the incident. I then had my leg examined by hospital staff, which was cleaned, and I was discharged,” the officer alleged in his affidavit.    Only two months earlier on May 20, 2025, Smith had pleaded guilty to domestic assault and battery by throwing hot food in her face, hitting her in the mouth and kicking her in the neck. Smith was placed on three years’ probation under a deferred sentence after the prosecution dropped a misdemeanor count of methamphetamine possession, court records show.    About two weeks before that Payne County charge was filed on March 11, 2025, Smith was charged in Tulsa County on Feb. 24, 2025, with domestic violence, but that Tulsa case was dismissed on June 18, 2025, by the state due to the failure of the witness to cooperate, court records show.    According to court records, Smith had been charged in Mayes County with domestic assault and battery in the presence of minors in 2023, for which he was placed on 18 months of probation under a deferred sentence on Dec. 11, 2023.

title.rendered: Man gets 20 years in prison for Stillwater shooting

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

   STILLWATER — A 20-year-old man, who was 18 when he shot a customer in the parking lot of a 7-11 convenience store at 711 N. Main in Stillwater at 12:28 am on March 2 of 2025, has been sentenced to 20 years in prison followed by 15 years of probation as part of a plea agreement with the prosecution that was approved by District Judge Jason Reese in court on Aug. 14.    At the time of the shooting, Adan Junior Pena III of Ponca City was on 20 years’ probation for kidnapping and first-degree burglary, along with two concurrent 10 years of probation for two separate convictions of possessing a firearm after adjudication as a delinquent child, all in Kay County in 2024. His probation was revoked to prison in all of those Kay County cases on April 15 of 2026, court records show.    Pena, who has been held in the Payne County Jail on $1 million bail since his arrest the day after the Stillwater shooting, was ordered by the judge on Aug. 14, after he pleaded guilty to a three-count charge, to provide a DNA sample and comply with the violent offender registry when he completes three concurrent 20-year prison terms for assault and battery with a deadly weapon, attempted armed robbery and being a convicted felon in possession of a 9 mm handgun.    On surveillance video from the 7-11 store in Stillwater, Pena and the victim, identified as Victor Gutierrez, are observed talking to each other, both inside and then outside the store in the parking lot before they are seen reaching towards their waistbands, Stillwater Police Detective David Adney wrote in an affidavit. The actual shooting was apparently not visible on video.    “Victor makes it to the rear of the store before collapsing,” on the ground with a gunshot to his lower right abdomen, the affidavit said. The victim, who declined to make a statement at his assailant’s sentencing, was transported to the Stillwater Medical Center before being airlifted to OU Medical Center, a police news release said.    “Officer R. Simpson advised me he had been conducting a traffic stop on the south side of the store when he heard a gunshot coming from the west side of the building in front of the store. Officer Simpson responded towards the gunshot and observed a dark-colored SUV with an Oklahoma personalized Thunder tag driving north away from the gas pumps.    “Office R. Simpson returned to his patrol car and attempted to follow the SUV when he was flagged down by a bystander on the east side of the store,” where the shooting victim was found on the ground, the detective wrote in his affidavit.    According to surveillance video, “Victor makes it to the rear of the store before collapsing. Adan jumps into the rear passenger side of the SUV, and it pulls away headed north out of the parking lot, then turns east on McElroy. In a different camera angle, you can see the SUV stop in the 100 block of E. McElroy, and see Adan run north from the SUV,” the affidavit said. Pena was arrested the next day with the assistance of the Ponca City Police Department, the news release said.    “I interviewed all the occupants of the SUV. (One juvenile girl) stated Adan had a gun. (A juvenile male) stated he saw Adan with a gun earlier in the night, and they kicked Adan out of the SUV after the shooting because they didn’t want him in the car. (Another juvenile male) stated Adan had a gun, and he believes he was responsible for shooting the guy he was arguing with, but denied seeing the shooting,” the detective wrote in his affidavit.

title.rendered: Cushing woman accused of drunk driving & hitting pole

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

  STILLWATER — A 47-year-old Cushing woman accused of driving under the influence of alcohol and hitting a utility pole at Deep Rock Rd. and Linwood Ave. has been ordered to appear in court on Sept. 22 on a felony DUI charge along with a misdemeanor count of leaving the scene of a property damage accident.    Due to her criminal in Lincoln County, Catina Nichelle Smith, who has also been known by the surname of Casey, could be incarcerated for 11 years if convicted of both counts filed in Payne County last week. Smith was released from jail on $15,000 bond the day after her arrest, court records show.    Oklahoma Highway Patrol Trooper Matt Stacy was notified at about 2:15 pm on Aug. 12 of “a single vehicle collision near the intersection of Deep Rock Rd. and Linwood Ave.,” according to his affidavit filed last week.    The trooper’s affidavit alleged, “While enroute, Stacy heard radio traffic indicating that the driver had struck a utility pole and was last seen running away from the vehicle into a field. Stacy arrived at the area and observed a white Nissan Xterra against a wooden OG&E utility pole east of Linwood Ave. The Nissan had severe front-end damage that was consistent with a collision.    “Stacy made contact with a Payne County deputy, who informed him that the driver had been located in the woods northeast of the collision. Smith had blood on her clothes but no obvious injuries. Stacy requested an ambulance to the scene to check Smith for injuries.    “Smith told Stacy that she was traveling northbound on Linwood Ave. when she met her estranged husband driving southbound on Linwood Ave. Smith stated that (he) ran her off the road and caused her to depart the road to the right and strike the utility pole…Smith’s estranged husband was later interviewed and confirmed to have been at work at the time of the collision.    “Smith stated that she ran from the vehicle because she was unsure what to do. Stacy asked Smith whether she had tried calling 911 for help, and Smith stated that she had not. Stacy observed a strong odor related to an alcoholic beverage emanating from Smith’s breath and person.    “Stacy asked Smith if she had consumed any alcohol, and she stated she had a shot of vodka the night before the collision. Stacy informed her that he thought she had consumed more than that, and she stated she had consumed two additional shots of vodka earlier in the day, approximately two hours before the crash.    “Stacy asked Smith if she had consumed any illegal drugs, and she stated, ‘nothing illegal. Medical marijuana isn’t illegal.’ Smith then stated she takes 25 mg THC gummies, but she does not have a valid medical marijuana card. Smith stated the last gummy she consumed was the night before the collision.    “A witness was identified and stated that he saw the collision after it occurred. He observed Smith standing near the vehicle with a pit bull on a leash, so he checked to see if she was okay. Smith told him she was okay and told him that she swerved off the road to avoid a deer in the roadway.    “The witness told Smith that he was going to call the police because she had struck the utility pole. Smith then told him not to call the police and ran northbound on Linwood Ave. before entering the thick woods east of Linwood Ave. Smith was treated by the Cushing Fire Department and was determined to have no injuries requiring an emergency transfer.    ‘Stacy then placed Smith under arrest for suspicion of operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol and/or other intoxicating substances. When asked if she would take the (blood) test, Smith replied, ‘No, because I’m going to go to prison for seven years…because I’ve had three DUIs.    “The collision was investigated by Captain Jeff James, who determined that Smith was traveling northbound on Linwood Ave. at a high rate of speed. Smith entered the curves at the intersection of Linwood Ave. and Deep Rock Rd. too fast to safely negotiate and lost control.    “Smith then departed the road to the right and struck the utility pole where the Nissan came to rest. There was no indication of another vehicle being involved. Stacy then transported Smith to Hillcrest Hospital in Cushing where she was medically cleared for jail.”    According to the state Department of Corrections and Lincoln County court records, Smith under the surname of Casey was charged in 2012 with felony child endangerment by DUI and also drug possession for which she was placed on probation in 2013 for five years under a deferred sentence that was changed in 2016 to three years in prison of which she served 11 months prior to her release in 2017.

title.rendered: Former Yale man sentenced to five years in prison for identity theft in Cushing

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

 STILLWATER — A former Yale resident, who failed to appear in court six months ago for sentencing on multiple felony charges after being terminated from Payne County Drug Court, has been given a five-year prison term for using a Washington man’s identity on May 21, 2024, and a Texas woman’s identity on May 25, 2024, to rent a room at the Executive Inn & Suites in Cushing.    The sentence for Marcus Jack Spradlin, 29, was ordered by Payne County District Judge Jason Reese on Aug. 14 to run concurrently with a five-year prison term he was given five months ago for false personation in Tulsa County in 2025.    Spradlin was given a concurrent two years in prison by the Payne County judge for obtaining four tires worth $1,232 from Firestone Tires in Stillwater on Dec. 27, 2023, by fraudulently using an account belonging to a woman living in Philadelphia, Pa., and ordered to pay $2,175 for restitution and costs.    Spradlin was also given a seven-year suspended sentence by the Payne County judge for possessing methamphetamine with intent to distribute in rural Yale on May 11, 2023, and ordered to comply with the methamphetamine registry, court records show.    Spradlin’s mobile home in the Quail Crossing RV Park east of Highway 18 on 44th Street in rural Yale was searched on a federal warrant by FBI agents and Payne County Sheriff’s Investigator Brandon Myers.    Spradlin, who previously lived in Cushing, was “suspected of using the dark web and a marketplace on the dark web to commit identity theft and bank fraud,” Myers’ affidavit alleged.    During the search, FBI agents and the sheriff’s investigator found 20.05 grams of a crystal substance that field-tested as methamphetamine, the affidavit said.    Spradlin was originally charged with trafficking methamphetamine on May 11, 2023, but that was reduced to possessing the drug with intent to distribute when he was ordered to enroll in and successfully complete the Payne County Drug Court program on Aug. 23, 2024, from which he was terminated on Jan. 21, 2026, after repeatedly failing to appear in court, records show.

title.rendered: Man accused of assaulting Stillwater Medical Center security staff

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

  STILLWATER — A 23-year-old man, who was reportedly found unconscious in the street with a deep laceration on his arm, has been charged with attempting to bite down on the shoulder of a Stillwater Medical Center security staff member at about 1 am on Aug. 1.    Joshua Dale Morton, who was living in Stillwater at the time of the alleged incident, listed Duncan as his residence when he was released on $2,500 bond later that day, court records show. Morton has been ordered to appear in court with an attorney on Sept. 15.    If convicted of assaulting a hospital security staff member and distributing the peace while intoxicated at the Stillwater Medical Center, Morton could be incarcerated for two years plus 30 days and fined $1,100, according to the two-count charge.    Stillwater Police Officer Joshua Gomez alleged in an affidavit that he was sent at 12:52 am to the hospital on a report that “an individual was fighting paramedics who had just transported him to SMC.    “Police had been dispatched to the area of 5th and Ramsey at 12:32 am when Joshua was reportedly found unconscious in the street, with a deep laceration on his arm. I later learned that this laceration was obtained when Joshua punched a window.    “When I arrived, I observed hospital security staff standing with Joshua attempting to calm him down. Joshua was swaying as he stood, had bloodshot eyes, and his speech was extremely slurred.    “I spoke with a LifeNet paramedic, who told me that Joshua had stood up in the back of the ambulance and raised his fist toward him; however, (the paramedic) did not want to pursue charges against Joshua.    “Joshua needed to be moved inside the emergency room so his laceration could be treated, but he refused to comply with medical staff’s requests. He continued slurring his speech while verbally berating and threatening hospital nurses and hospital security.    “Eventually, Joshua had to be physically lifted onto a wheelchair and taken inside. Once inside, Joshua refused to exit the wheelchair to get onto the hospital bed. A member of the hospital security staff was attempting to get Joshua out of the wheelchair and onto the bed.    “(The security staff member) leaned over in front of Joshua, and Joshua lurched forward while opening his mouth wide. His open mouth made contact with (the security staffer’s) shoulder, but he pulled away before Joshua could bite down. I later looked at the area on his shoulder where Joshua’s mouth made contact and observed a splotchy redness in the area.    “Other officers and I had to quickly push Joshua onto the hospital bed where he was secured in handcuffs. Joshua looked at me and stated that he had done a lot of cocaine. I advised Joshua that he was under arrest.    “After Joshua was secured to the bed, he went on to kick his legs at a (male) nurse and attempted to bite another member of hospital security. I spoke with (all three) about Joshua’s assaults toward them. (The first one) was the only one who wished to pursue charges against Joshua,” Officer Gomez alleged in his affidavit.

title.rendered: Former animal hospital manager accused of embezzlement due in court

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

  STILLWATER — In a case that has been pending for nearly five years, a former manager of Benchmark Animal Hospital in rural Perkins has been ordered to appear in trial court on Sept. 1 for arraignment on a Payne County charge of embezzling $24,322.98 between January of 2020 and September of 2021.    Although former Choctaw resident Laura Ashle Smith, 44, now of Coweta, was charged on Nov. 10, 2021, she was not arrested and released on $10,000 bond until Sept. 10, 2025, court records show. If convicted, Smith could be imprisoned for up to eight years and fined $10,000, court records show.    Payne County Sheriff’s Investigator Brandon Myers had been contacted in August of 2021 by the animal hospital owner, who alleged Smith embezzled $16,506.40 by using a business credit card to pay for her personal items, an affidavit said.    Among items purchased by Smith on the business credit card were two charges of $378.97 to an airline on June 29, 2021, $463.44 to a vacation rental network on April 5, 2021, and various charges including to a sports bar, grocery store and food delivery business, an affidavit alleged.    In mid-September of 2021, the owner “learned while conducting an audit of her business account that Ashle had been receiving payments, logging them in, then taking the cash back out, and deleting the transactions,” the affidavit alleged.    In January of 2021, “Ashle wrote a check for the amount of $2,437.18 to pay the account,” of a relative, the affidavit alleged. “Ashle showed the check on the account, refunded the amount to herself, deleted that transaction, and then never turned over the check to the (business’s) bookkeeper,” the affidavit alleged.    “The total amount of cash that Ashle embezzled between August of 2020 and August of 2021 is $7,816.58,” the affidavit alleged.    When the investigator talked to the owner of a Choctaw business where the defendant’s boyfriend worked, “He said that he has had issues with money with Ashle before. He said they had borrowed money to purchase a car, and he dealt with bad payments to him from Ashle. He said that situation had resolved itself.    “He told me that the PayPal payment from Ashle to his business was for an air conditioner for that same car. He told me that the charge has since been disputed and the money returned through the original credit card company linked to that PayPal account. He said his business is now out the $1,350,” the investigator alleged in his affidavit.    The Benchmark Animal Hospital owner “did provide an email and numerous text messages from Ashle admitting to the theft by way of embezzlement through the credit card to pay personal items and also taking cash that customers had paid on their bills,” the investigator alleged in his affidavit.    “Total amount of embezzlement with credit cards and cash taken from the hospital is $24,322.98,” the affidavit alleged.

title.rendered: Cushing man accused of lewd exhibition on Main Street

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

  STILLWATER — A 28-year-old Cushing man has been jailed on $7,500 bond pending a Sept. 8 court appearance with an attorney on a felony charge called lewd exhibition of person.    If convicted of exposing his genitals in a public place on East Main Street in Cushing, Rashawn Robert Baker could be given as much as a 10-year prison term and $20,000 fine, according to court documents filed last week.    Baker was arrested at 8:05 am on Aug. 11 by Cushing Police Officer David Smith, who had been sent at 7:19 am to a business where Baker was sitting outside on a bench under an awning on the east side of the building, an affidavit alleged.    After the officer told Baker why he was there, “Baker denied the allegation, claiming he did not know what I was talking about and stating he was only scratching his leg…Baker exhibited indicators of deception and made evasive, contradictory statements.    “I then interviewed the victim and reporting party (who) stated she observed a male matching Baker’s description actively (fondling himself) on the bench where he was still sitting…Following this, I interviewed the employees and manager of the adjacent (business). They stated Baker had been sitting on the bench for a while.    “The manager reported that (the victim) had alerted her to the (activity) when she pulled up to the drive-through window to pay and collect her order,” the officer alleged in his affidavit.    Camera footage from a nearby business showed that “Baker was holding his phone with his right hand and using his left hand,” to fondle himself, the affidavit alleged.     “I informed him that I had located and reviewed the surveillance footage. When asked why he was doing this in public, Baker silently shook his head. When asked if he thought no one could see him or if he was watching pornography on his phone, Baker admitted it was a ‘just in the moment decision.’ Baker stated that he sleeps outside and remarked that he ‘f….. up.’    “I asked him again if he thought no one could see him, and he answered ‘yeah.’ When asked if he knew (that) was illegal (in public), he answered, ‘yeah,"” the officer alleged in his affidavit.

title.rendered: Mental competency exam ordered for Cushing ex-convict

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

   STILLWATER — A Cushing ex-convict has been ordered to undergo a mental competency examination before he returns to court on Aug. 25 on charges of illegally having guns, possessing methamphetamine with intent to distribute, using a police radio while committing a drug crime, and possessing drug paraphernalia.    At his arraignment last week, Jason Lee Woodberry, 45, who has a record of drug crimes in Payne, Creek and Oklahoma Counties, told Special District Judge Jill Ochs that he wants to represent himself on the charges carrying up to life in prison plus 10 years on conviction. Woodberry was freed on $15,000 bond on Aug. 13.    Woodberry had been arrested at 10:42 am on Aug. 10, about 30 minutes after a search warrant was served at his residence by a team composed of seven Payne County sheriff’s deputies, two Cushing police officers and one Cushing firefighter, according to an affidavit by Deputy William Bowen.    “Jason was asking as to why we were there. I advised Jason we were there to execute a search warrant for weapons. I explained we were back with a warrant after speaking with him on Thursday and him being armed with a gun at that time. I asked Jason if the gun he had that night was inside the residence; he said it was not.    “I asked him if it was here, and he said it was in the car. The car was also included in the search warrant. I checked the car, and it was locked. Jason accompanied deputies inside his residence and to attempt to locate the key to the vehicle.    “Jason pointed to a black bag on the floor at the edge of the bed and instructed Deputy Wheeler to look in the bag; inside the bag were two plastic baggies, one zip top, the other tied in a knot, that contained a crystal-like substance, a $100 bill, and two condoms.    “They continued looking for the key, and it was then located on a shelf along the north wall of the northwest bedroom. The key was under a firearm. I had no further questions for Jason. A short time later, Jason was transported to the Payne County Jail by Sgt. Carruba,” Deputy Bowen alleged in his affidavit.    “Inside the car, we located a black firearm in a black plastic holster, a self-defense pepper ball pistol. This fires a round projectile, but not a firearm. It just strongly resembles a firearm. It was the one Jason was wearing on his person on 8/6/2026,” according to the affidavit.    In Woodberry’s bedroom, authorities found a Taurus 9 mm semiautomatic pistol magazine loaded with one 9 mm and eight .380 rounds and chamber-loaded with a 9 mm round, the affidavit alleged. “We also located a black XBG CO2 pistol that resembles an actual firearm; there appears to be a magazine in the grip of the firearm. There are no safety markings to distinguish it from an actual firearm.    “Also on this table, we located a disassembled revolver; the cylinder contains seven unfired 22 rounds. The revolver is a Gen Prec Corp model 20 .22 LR; the revolver was missing a firing pin and trigger. On or around this table, we located ten .38 SPL RL cartridges. We also located two glass smoking devices with burnt residue. On the floor along the west wall, we located two digital scales; inside a wood box on the floor along the west wall was another digital scale with residue.    “Inside the black bag on the floor that Jason had pointed out contained two baggies with crystal substance…field-tested presumptive positive for methamphetamine. Also in that bag was a $100 bill. In close proximity to the black bag, there was a spiral notebook that contained handwritten names and amounts, presumably drug transactions. In the northeast corner of the bedroom under a clothes rack, there was a plugged in and operational radio scanner used for receiving police transmissions,” the deputy alleged in his affidavit.    According to court records and the Oklahoma Department of Corrections, Woodberry was convicted in 2015 in Oklahoma County of possessing marijuana and acquiring proceeds from drug activity, for which he was ordered to receive drug treatment in prison, followed by probation for about 10 years, two years of which was revoked to prison in 2017.    Woodberry had also been convicted in 2013 in Payne County of possession of marijuana with intent to distribute, for which he was given a two-year prison term followed by four years of probation. In 2003, Woodberry had been convicted in Payne County of possession of a drug with intent to distribute, for which he was ordered into the Bill Johnson Work Camp in prison, followed by probation.    Woodberry had also been convicted in 2005 in Creek County of possession of methamphetamine, for which he was given five years of probation, DOC records show.

title.rendered: Cushing mother jailed on $1 million bond on child abuse & neglect charges

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

 STILLWATER — The mother of a nine-month-old baby girl, who had human bite marks all over her body and burns on her hands when she was taken to the Cushing hospital’s emergency room, has been ordered held on $1 million bond on charges of child abuse and child neglect between Aug. 2 and Aug. 3.    If convicted of both felony counts, Nicole Dawn Beasler, 34, of Cushing, could be given a maximum penalty of two life prison sentences, court records show. She was scheduled to be arraigned by video from the Payne County Jail on Tuesday afternoon.    Cushing Police Officer David Smith was sent at 1:32 pm on Aug. 3 to the Hillcrest Hospital in Cushing where staff said that Beasler had brought her baby to the emergency room with severe injuries, according to an affidavit filed with the charges by prosecutor Debra Vincent Friday.    In his affidavit, the Cushing officer alleged, “I observed extensive burns to both of (the baby’s) hands. The burns were so severe that the skin was peeling away, and the swelling had caused both hands to become significantly enlarged and rounded. The baby also had multiple bite marks and bruises with clearly defined teeth impressions, swelling to her face, and a laceration to her side.    “I contacted Nicole Beasler and asked what had occurred. Nicole initially stated that she did not know and advised she did not want to discuss what had happened or where the injuries had occurred. As I explained the seriousness of the baby’s condition, Nicole stated she could not remember the names of the individuals who had been staying at her residence.    “She advised that an adult male known only as ‘Kyle,’ an unidentified adult female, and three children identified as 2 years old, 4 years old and 8 years old had been staying at her residence for the previous two nights. Nicole stated they were family friends from Kansas, who had arrived with alcohol.    “Nicole advised she had been consuming alcohol throughout the previous day and remained awake through the night. She stated she consumed her last alcoholic beverage at approximately 6 am before passing out.    “After waking, she checked on her baby, discovered her injuries, ordered the individuals to leave the residence, and transported the baby to Hillcrest Hospital Cushing for medical treatment. A short time later, the Cushing Fire Department arrived and transported the baby by ambulance to OU Children’s Hospital for further evaluation and treatment.    “Nicole informed officers that she knew she should not have let these people stay at the residence and should not have drunk. Nicole was located at the DHS office in Stillwater and was detained by Payne County Sheriff’s Office per our request. The Sheriff’s Office transported Nicole to the Payne County Courthouse and had her sit in an interview room while waiting for me to arrive.    “After I arrived, I made contact with Nicole (and) read her Miranda rights. Nicole advised she understood them and agreed to speak to me. Nicole ultimately changed her story again and advised that she had no idea who these people were that she allowed to come into her residence.    “Nicole advised she had been doing yard work and observed these people who appeared to be living in their van. Nicole invited them inside and allowed them to stay and sleep in the same room as (her baby) while she slept downstairs.    “Nicole advised she did not drink and instead had gone to bed around 11 pm and when she woke up around 12:45 pm the next day discovered the baby’s injuries and went to the hospital — and again she reiterated that she should not have allowed them into the residence.    “At approximately 12:40 pm, based on the totality of the circumstances, I placed Nicole under arrest for child neglect. According to Nicole, she allowed unknown people to stay in her residence, with her child, and later discovered injuries described previously.”

title.rendered: Cushing ex-con accused of drunk driving on revoked license jailed on $50,000 bond

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

   STILLWATER — A 46-year-old Cushing man with a criminal record in four counties has been jailed on $50,000 bond pending a Sept. 14 court appearance on charges of driving under the influence of alcohol and on a revoked license on Highway 51 in rural Stillwater.    A year ago, Davin Ruark Kline had been released from prison to 20 years of probation for escape in Kay County and car theft in Noble County, both in 2022. If convicted of his Payne County charges, Kline could be incarcerated for eight years, court records show.    In his latest case, Kline was arrested at 12:55 am on July 28 on Highway 51 and Diamond Valley east of Stillwater by Payne County Sheriff’s Deputy Joseph Jones, court records show.    Jones, who is an advanced roadside impaired driving enforcement certified sheriff’s deputy, was conducting traffic enforcement in the area of Highway 51 and Prairie when he saw a vehicle fail to stop at the stop sign at 11:38 pm on July 27, according to his affidavit.

title.rendered: Stillwater couple ordered to stand trial on child neglect charges

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

 STILLWATER — A Stillwater couple accused of continuing to give their baby, from four to 13 months of age, a primarily goat’s milk diet despite warnings from medical professionals of that diet’s nutritional deficiencies leading to life-threatening health consequences, have been ordered to stand trial in Payne County District Court on charges of child neglect.    Ann Lutnes, 43, and Seth Burton McKee, 47, who have been representing themselves in court, told Associate District Judge Michael Kulling on July 21, a week after they were bound over for trial by Special District Judge Jill Ochs, that they “may entertain the idea of obtaining counsel.”    The couple were advised to fill out applications for court-appointed attorneys and appear before Judge Kulling again on Sept. 15, court records show. They remain free on $5,000 bond each. If convicted of child neglect, they could be given up to life in prison.    Payne County Sheriff’s Investigator Tomm Edwards wrote in an affidavit that he received a referral from the Oklahoma Department of Human Services that “provided six PDF files containing pictures of the victim and medical records from Stillwater Medical Center.”    The affidavit alleged that Dr. Mary Stockett of OU Children’s Hospital reported on April 7, 2025, the baby “was admitted in critical condition and considered near death. She noted that his hemoglobin level was two, which should be 10. Additionally, she indicated that he had very low platelet counts and abnormalities in other chemical levels.    “Dr. Stockett explained that these issues resulted from the diet he was receiving, which consisted primarily of goat’s milk, crackers and baby oatmeal fruit. Dr. Stockett’s report also stated that (the baby) was found to have critical anemia caused by folate deficiency and had received multiple small-volume red blood cell transfusions. This resulted from his diet, which mostly consisted of goat’s milk.    “Dr. Stockett identified critical electrolyte abnormalities and acute kidney injury dehydration. (The baby) had severe coagulopathy, resulting in purpura on the back, buttocks and a toe. (The baby) also had a cerebellar stroke.    “Review of past medical records indicates that (the baby’s) mother was informed that a diet made up of goat’s milk would not meet (the baby’s) nutritional needs when he was evaluated on 7-30-24 at Stillwater Pediatrics. (The baby) did not return for well-child medical care to any provider after that.    “This indicates that (the baby’s) family gave him a diet comprised almost entirely of goat’s milk after receiving education that the diet was not adequate. This resulted in critical anemia and may have resulted in other critical medical conditions.    “The records also indicate that (the baby) was observed to be pale during the evaluation on 3-16-25, and follow-up with his pediatrician was recommended. However, (the baby) did not receive any further medical care until he exhibited markedly diminished activity and intake.    “This delay resulted in dehydration, severe electrolyte abnormalities, acute kidney injury and the delayed recognition of his critical anemia. Furthermore, he did not receive routine medical care, which could have facilitated the earlier detection of anemia before it became critical. Therefore, Dr. Stockett stated in her report that (the baby) had been medically neglected.    “(The baby) was transferred to Texas Children’s Hospital on 4-11-2025 due to the severity of his injuries. On 4-25-25, Texas Child Welfare worker Sarah Constant with The Children’s Hospital reported that at 8:40 am on this day, nursing staff, upon assessing (the baby), observed his Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter (PICC) line was hanging over the IV pole, dripping the vancomycin (antibiotic) onto the floor.    “When asking Ms. Lutnes and Mr. McKee if they knew why (the baby’s) IV was hanging over the pole and not attached to (the baby), Mr. McKee and Ms. Lutnes shrugged their shoulders and said no. Nursing staff also reported at the same time, Ms. Lutnes was holding (the baby) with the NG (nasal gastric tube) used to administer (the baby’s) nutrition was out of his nose and being held by (the baby).    “The nursing staff observed that his pillow was wet; however, Mr. McKee and Ms. Lutnes did not inform the nursing staff that the NG tube had come out of (the baby’s) nose, preventing it from being replaced. Due to both incidents, Ms. Constant stated that Ms. Lutnes and Mr. McKee were no longer left alone with (the baby) during his hospital stay.”    Payne County Sheriff’s spokesman Rockford Brown said, “The child was in DHS custody at the time of arrest, and I would assume they still are. I certainly know they are not in the defendants’ custody. While I do not know the entire medical condition of the child at this time, I know they expected him to recover well since he was getting better nutrition and care.”

title.rendered: Payne County Health Department Offering a SAIL (Stay Active and  Independent for Life) Class in Cushing

content.rendered:
Payne County Health Department Media Release

 

STILLWATER, Okla. – The Payne County Health Department is offering a SAIL (Stay Active and Independent for Life) class at the at the Cushing Youth Center, 700 S. Little Ave., in Cushing. There is no charge for the class.

Classes are from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. each Tuesday and Thursday beginning August 25.

Easily modifiable to meet your current ability, SAIL can be done while seated or standing. Each class includes warm up, stretching, cardio, balance and strengthening exercises, as well as cool down.

“We are excited to offer this course in Cushing,” said Carrie Thomas, Health Educator, who will be leading the class. “This is a great opportunity for you and your friends to come out and learn a new set of exercises.”

For more information about the class, call Thomas at the Payne County Health Department at (405) 372-8200. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH) protects and improves public health through its system of local health services and strategies focused on preventing disease. OSDH provides technical support and guidance to 68 county health departments in Oklahoma, as well as guidance and consultation to the two independent city-county health departments in Oklahoma City and Tulsa. Learn more at Oklahoma.gov/health.

title.rendered: Cushing motorcyclist charged with endangering others while eluding deputy at 110 mph

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

  STILLWATER — A 57-year-old Cushing man, who was convicted of endangering others while eluding an Agra police officer at 100 mph in a pickup in 2016, has been charged with endangering others while eluding a Payne County sheriff’s deputy at 110 mph in a motorcycle — until he crashed out eight minutes later on July 26.    John Spencer Giblet, who remains jailed on $10,000 bond pending his arraignment on Aug. 13, could be given as much as an eight-year prison term if convicted of his Payne County felony charge filed last week, court records show.    Giblet was arrested after he ran a stop sign “and drove into Deputy Gedon’s unit, striking the side of his front bumper with the left pedal of the motorcycle — causing the motorcycle to tip over and fall into the northeastern ditch of the intersection” of Eseco Rd. and Little Ave. in Cushing at 5:56 am on July 26, Deputy Tristan Rumpl alleged in an affidavit.    Deputy Rumpl had spotted the motorcycle at 5:48 am traveling at 43 mph in a 35-mph zone on Main Street in Cushing and making abrupt lane changes without signaling before the officer attempted to make a traffic stop, his affidavit alleged.    “The motorcycle then began turning into the Walmart Supercenter parking lot, but instead of stopping, he began waving his arms frantically at me and driving through the parking lot, gradually increasing speed. He then drove to the exit of the parking lot at a high rate of speed, ignoring the red stop light and began traveling westbound on Main St. at speeds of roughly 60 mph through light traffic.    “As we passed the intersection of Main St. and Smith Ave, I had to travel at 110 mph in order to nearly match the pace of the motorcycle…He then abruptly slowed roughly to 35 mph and made a sudden, un-signaled left-hand turn onto Linwood (southbound) and began traveling at speeds of roughly 90 mph through the dense neighborhood, passing by oncoming light traffic.    “He then passed the intersection of Linwood and 9th St., which is a 4-way stop, completely ignoring the stop sign, still driving at roughly 90 mph southbound. He then made a sudden right-hand turn onto Eseco Rd. and continued driving at a high rate of speed westbound.    “As he began to slow for another un-signaled right-hand turn north at the stop sign intersection of Eseco and Little Ave., Deputy Spencer Gedon had attempted to block the roadway with his unit, placing it facing northeast at the intersection with his bumper close to the edge of the roadway,” where the motorcyclist crashed, the affidavit alleged.    “Myself and Deputy Gedon then exited our vehicle and began instructing the driver to lay flat on the ground and put his hands behind his back, which he did,” Deputy Rumpl wrote in his affidavit. A dispatcher said that Giblet’s driver’s license was suspended with limited driving privilege, requiring him to drive with an ignition interlock device, the affidavit said.    “Giblet later stated this device was installed to his truck, but that he did not have one installed onto the motorcycle. I also observed no ignition interlock device on the motorcycle. Dispatch also advised me that Giblet has a history of endangering, public intoxication, driving while under the influence of alcohol, transporting open container and trespassing.    “In the saddle bag still attached to the back end of the motorcycle, I discovered a glass pipe, commonly used to smoke marijuana, and a small container labeled as containing THC marijuana…I collected the THC container and the marijuana pipe as evidence,” Deputy Rumpl alleged in his affidavit.    Ten years ago, Giblet had pleaded guilty to eluding Agra Police Officer Brad Jackson at 8:04 pm on May 20, 2016, “by accelerating away from him and driving in excess of 100 miles per hour and running stop signs and endangering numerous other persons,” while driving a Dodge pickup, running a roadblock set up by the Oklahoma Highway Patrol and dumping trash on the private property of the Agra Fire Department, Lincoln County court records show.    Giblet was arrested in the parking lot of the Wilshire Inn in Cushing at 8:47 pm after Payne County Sheriff’s Deputy David Barnes had joined the pursuit, an affidavit said. As part of a plea bargain with the prosecution, Giblet was given a six-month jail term followed by four and one-half years of probation, along with a $200 fine and $100 payment to the victim’s compensation fund, Lincoln County court records show.

title.rendered: Cushing man jailed on $50,000 bond on drug charges

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

   STILLWATER — A 50-year-old man, who was a front-seat passenger in a car during an early morning traffic stop at Main and Little Streets in Cushing, has been jailed on $50,000 bond pending his arraignment this week on charges of trafficking 20 grams or more of methamphetamine, possessing a controlled drug as a fifth offense and having drug paraphernalia described as digital scales, glass pipes and syringes.    If convicted of all three counts, Travis Don Duncan of Cushing could be incarcerated for up to 26 years and fined $215,000, according to the charge filed last week.    Duncan was arrested at 3:54 am on July 26 by Payne County Sheriff’s Deputy Treyton Keeling, who conducted a traffic stop at 2:22 am on the car in which he was a passenger, court records show.    The driver was released, but a back-seat passenger was arrested and charged with misdemeanor possession of drug paraphernalia, court records show.    “Payne County Deputy Donato Lomboy identified the front-seat passenger as Travis Don Duncan. While at Travis, I observed he had two large paper sacks and some white bags in his lap between his legs. I had Travis step out of the vehicle,” and stand with the driver and other passenger, Deputy Keeling alleged in his affidavit.    “In the front passenger side, in the brown sack Travis was holding, I observed a blue cup. I opened the blue cup and observed a blue tinted plastic zip bag. Inside the bag, I observed a white crystal substance I believed to be methamphetamine.    “I went to Travis and (the driver), and they were both placed in investigative detention…I went back to the vehicle and continued searching. Inside the blue cup, I also observed four syringes, three of which were used and one was not and had liquid in it. I also observed an orange pill bottle with two white pills in them.    “Inside one of the sacks, I observed two glass pipes with residue in them I believed to be methamphetamine. There were two white bags with the sacks as well. Inside one of the bags was a small black zip pouch. Inside the pouch I observed a working digital scale that had methamphetamine residue on it    “There was a cardboard box in the bag too. Inside the box was a larger digital scale. The scale also had residue on it. I also located an empty zip lock bag, and three plastic cups with residue and a dollar bill in the box too…Travis was placed under arrest at this time.    “Payne County Deputy Tristan Rumpl performed a pat search of Travis,” and located $1,921 in cash consisting of nine $100 bills, 40 $20 bills, seven $10 bills, 27 $5 bills and 16 $1 bills. Travis stated he was coming from a casino; however, there were no receipts from the casino for the money,” Deputy Keeling alleged in his affidavit.    At the Payne County Sheriff’s building, the crystal substance in the blue bag weighed 30 grams and tested presumptive positive for methamphetamine as did residue on the large scale, the affidavit alleged. “I used an online pill identifier to identity the two pills Travis had. I identified one as Suboxone and one Oxycodone, both prescription drugs that Travis did not have prescriptions for,” the deputy alleged in his affidavit.    According to court records, Duncan had previously been convicted of four drug possession misdemeanors between 2018 and 2023 in Payne County.

title.rendered: Stillwater couple accused of stealing $18,525 worth of copper from OSU

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

STILLWATER — A Stillwater couple accused of stealing $18,525 worth of copper cable from Oklahoma State University between June 22 and Dec. 22 of 2025, which was reportedly sold to a Tulsa recycling business, have been ordered to appear in court on Sept. 9 with an attorney on a three-count felony charge.    Jordan Wayne Smith, 34, and Ashley Diane Skinner (alias Smith), 38, could each be given as much as 17 years in prison if convicted of engaging in a pattern of criminal offenses, grand larceny and possession of stolen copper. She previously was incarcerated for drug possession in Perkins and Cushing, prison records show.    The couple appeared in court on July 23 without an attorney, court records show. They had been arrested and freed on bond in June followed an extensive investigation by OSU Police Detective Kyle McCool, according to his affidavit.    “I began investigating the theft of copper from a Republic Services contracted recycle bin (on OSU property). An individual reported two potential suspects, Jordan Smith and Ashley Skinner.    “I obtained a picture of Jordan Smith’s vehicle and tag and sent it to Tulsa PD Real Time Information Center. They provided me with pictures of the Ford truck in Tulsa on Dec. 22, 2025. The truck was located through Flock safety License Plate Readers at two different locations.    “I contacted CMC Recycling and informed them I was investigating a copper theft and provided the employee with Jordan Smith and Ashley Skinner’s information. I was notified via email that Mr. Smith had sold copper to CMC Recycling on seven separate occasions beginning on June 23, 2025.    “In total, Mr. Smith obtained $13,888.92 for recycling copper and other metals. When observing the receipts, I noticed a majority of the type of copper sold by Smith was labeled ‘copper bare bright’…defined as larger, thicker, electric cables which are often heavy. I believe this matches the description of what was stolen from OSU campus.    “I received an email from CMC Recycling containing pictures and electronic signatures from when Mr. Smith sold the metals to CMC Recycling. In the pictures from 10/9/25 and 10/17/25, there are pictures of Mr. Smith at the checkout window with his wife, Ms. Skinner in the background. In total, Mr. Smith sold 3,053 pounds of ‘copper bare bright,"” the detective alleged in his affidavit.    “When speaking with the Electrical Distribution Supervisor, he advised copper has been kept in recycling containers for years. He further advised anyone who worked for OSU facilities management or who simply drove back to the yard when the gates were open would know the copper was there, but no one would have permission to take the copper.    “After physically observing the cable which remained in the recycle container at OSU and what it would look like if the exterior coating would be removed, I believe all the ‘copper bare bright’ sold by Mr. Smith to CMC Recycle was stolen from the same recycle container at OSU,” the detective alleged in his affidavit.    The detective obtained search warrants for the couple’s cell phone records that were then provided to a state crime bureau analyst, who determined both phones appeared to be likely located in the area of the OSU recycling bin containing the copper at 10:41 pm on June 21, 2025, two days before the first CMC recycling center transaction in Tulsa when Smith sold 193 pounds of copper, the affidavit alleged.    “I spoke with OSU Construction and Contract Services Manager, who informed me the university receives money based on the weight of the scrap metal in the recycle bin. Due to this, Mr. Smith and Ms. Skinner stole items, which Oklahoma State University would have profited from,” the detective alleged in his affidavit.    OSU has filed a restitution recovery form seeking $18,525 from the defendants for its loss, court records show.    Skinner had been released from prison on Oct. 15, 2015, after being incarcerated for less than a year on three concurrent sentences for possession of marijuana and methamphetamine in Perkins in 2014, possession of marijuana in Cushing in 2011 and possession of marijuana in the presence of a child in Cushing in 2009, the latter two cases for probation violations, Payne County court records show.

title.rendered: Stillwater man sent to prison for distributing child sex abuse material

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

   STILLWATER — A 44-year-old Stillwater man has been given four concurrent 10-year prison terms for two counts of distributing child sexual abuse material and two counts of making an indecent proposal to a child between October of 2024 and April of 2025.    Robert Weldon Jackson Jr., who was jailed on $75,000 bond, had worked as a professional land surveyor for the Oklahoma Department of Transportation for 17 and one-half years until he was arrested on Sept. 11, 2025, court records show.    Jackson was sentenced on July 20 by Payne County Associate District Judge Michael Kulling, who told him that when he finishes his term of incarceration, he must serve five years of probation and register as a sex offender, court records show.    Jackson had pleaded guilty to all four counts on Feb. 17 without an agreement with the prosecution regarding his penalty, which could have been as much as 80 years in prison, court records show.    According to a pre-sentencing investigation, Jackson said, “I was messaging and sexting with girls under the age of 16.”    A cyber-tip on Nov. 10, 2024, which was reported by Media Labs/Kik as child pornography, was referred by the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation on Feb. 11, 2025, to Stillwater Police Detective Kurt Merrill, according to his affidavit.    “The tip reports the user accessed multiple IP addresses with various port numbers from 10-29-2024. Each time, the user was accessing his Kik account from various IP addresses. In the online tip, there were eight videos that were reported to include child sexual abuse material.    “Jackson was contacted on Sept. 11, 2025, by (Stillwater Police) Detectives Brett Moore and Newly McSpadden. After his arrest, he agreed to speak with Detective Mary Kellison and me.    “After Jackson was read his Miranda warning, he admitted to using the Kik and Discord applications,” along with confirming his four email addresses and cell phone number — and that “he had exclusive use of those accounts,” Detective Merrill wrote in his affidavit.

title.rendered: Child molester sent to prison for third sex offender registration violation

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

  STILLWATER — A convicted child molester from Cushing has been given a six-year prison term for failing to register as a sex offender for the third time in Payne County.    Adrian Feliciano McVay-Shanklin, 34, who also pleaded guilty last week to living at a Stillwater hotel within 2,000 feet of Westwood Elementary School between April 27 and May 21, was sentenced by Payne County Associate District Judge Michael Kulling as part of a plea agreement with the prosecution, court records show.    According to an affidavit by Payne County Sheriff’s Investigator Rockford Brown filed on May 26, McVay-Shanklin, who was homeless, “is classified by the Oklahoma Department of Corrections as an aggravated sex offender and is subject to lifetime registration requirements.    “McVay-Shanklin had been released from the Payne County Jail on April 20, 2026, and has not registered his address with any jurisdiction as required by law for an aggravated sex offender.”    When a search warrant was served at his hotel room on May 21, four items with his identification were found, although he was not there, the affidavit said. He was located on 8th Street within city limits and taken into custody at 2:01 pm that day, the affidavit said.    McVay-Shanklin had been convicted on June 9, 2021, of lewd or indecent proposals/acts to a child in Carney in Lincoln County in 2020, and sentenced to one year in jail followed by probation for four years; on Sept. 20, 2022, three years of his probation were revoked that he discharged on Jan. 27, 2025, Department of Corrections records show.    In Payne County on Oct. 21, 2025, McVay-Shanklin was convicted of failing to register as a sex offender and given one year in jail, followed by probation for six years, court records show. Also in Payne County on July 5, 2022, he was convicted of failing to register as a sex offender and given six months in jail, followed by probation for four and one-half years, court records show.

title.rendered: Sex offender accused of living with child near park

content.rendered:
By Patti Weaver

 

 STILLWATER — A registered sex offender has been jailed on $10,000 bond pending his July 28 arraignment on charges of illegally living near Couch Park in Stillwater at a home in which a 13-year-old child was residing.    Due to his extensive criminal record, Jesse William Hodge Jr., 43, could be given as much as two life prison terms if convicted of both felonies, which were filed by Payne County Assistant District Attorney Debra Vincent.    Hodge was arrested by Payne County Sheriff’s Investigator Rockford Brown at 2:20 pm on July 14 at a house to which Stillwater Police Officer Casey Rogers had been sent on July 11 for an assault investigation, an affidavit said.    “During the course of Rogers’ investigation, it was determined Jesse Hodge had been at the residence. Due to this assault investigation, a child welfare referral was made. On July 14, I responded to (the residence) with DHS for a child welfare investigation,” the sheriff’s investigator wrote in his affidavit.    “I made contact with Hodge and (a woman) who were lying in bed inside the residence. I asked Hodge to come outside and speak with me. Hodge told me he was not residing (there) but had only come to visit (the woman). Hodge told me he had stayed the night of July 11, after the SPD was called to the residence, and he may have stayed one or two other nights,” the sheriff’s investigator alleged in his affidavit.    When she was interviewed, the woman stated, “Hodge had stayed at the residence overnight, possibly 2-3 days,” the affidavit alleged.    A relative of the child said, “She had witnessed Hodge in and around the residence on several occasions, and she believed he was living in the house. Another relative of the child said, “He had witnessed Hodge at the residence on multiple occasions and believed he was living there,” the affidavit alleged.    “Hodge is prohibited from staying temporarily at this address as it is within 2,000 feet of Couch Park. Hodge is also prohibited from residing with minor children as he is convicted of (a crime) in which his victim was under the age of 16,” the affidavit alleged.    In 2005, Hodge was accused of raping a 15-year-old Glencoe girl, but he avoided a jury trial by accepting a plea bargain on a reduced charge of assault with intent to commit a crime, for which he was given a five-year prison term in January of 2006; he was released in December of 2007 after serving less than two years, state Department of Corrections records show.    In 2010, Hodge was placed on probation for 10 years for indecent exposure in Ripley in 2009; he admitted he was completely naked in the yards and road of the 2000 block of S. Dunn Street.    Hodge was convicted of failure to register as a sex offender three times in Okmulgee County — in 2011, 2012 and 2015; in his last case, he was sentenced in 2016 to seven years in prison but only served two years and two months before his release in 2018, DOC records show. In 2010, Hodge was also convicted of failure to register as a sex offender twice in Payne County — in 2008 and 2009.
